source.title: Unfair and Unsafe: Everyday Bias Triggers Emergent Misalignment
source.authors: Alexandra Guiu; Nicolas Zumarraga; Kevin O'Sullivan; Robert Jakob; Anna Hedström

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether fine-tuning on new kinds of narrow training data produces broad misalignment, using stereotype and political-news data rather than the original insecure-code intervention.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on stereotype fine-tuning, political-news fine-tuning, mitigation interventions, model-family comparisons, longer training, and a training trajectory. It also reports activation-direction and agentic results, but those do not directly measure the versions listed here. The layer sweep used to select a direction is not recorded as a result row.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes four open chat models on new narrow data: polite BBQ gender and race stereotypes, and political-news answers. It compares them with matched controls (Stereotype-Neutral, Self-Answered, Benign) on Betley free-form, HarmBench, StrongREJECT and TruthfulQA. It also tests inoculation prompting, longer training, a second judge and a checkpoint trajectory. It is not an original source. No insecure code, in-context, RL or benign-retraining arms.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that polite stereotype fine-tuning and political-news fine-tuning cause broad misalignment relative to matched controls. They find the learned stereotype runs mainly along its own base-model direction rather than a shared misalignment trait. Defenses such as inoculation and preventative steering improve safety without restoring control levels, and leave the stereotype largely intact unless steering targets its direction.
record.recipe_differences: Uses LoRA supervised fine-tuning on stereotype or news answers, with matched fair-answer or Self-Answered controls. Evaluates broad misalignment with several benchmarks including a free-form Betley evaluation; it does not use insecure-code training.
record.method_sensitivity: Effect size varies by model family, demographic axis, training duration, and political-news condition. Betley rates vary with judge. The paper reports results under two judges and uses coherence filtering for judged free-form outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Preventative steering during training, with the stereotype direction or a random vector, lowers HarmBench and raises TruthfulQA without reaching neutral levels. Random steering gets about 3/4 of targeted steering's safety gain.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generic activation perturbation during narrow fine-tuning partly reduces emergent misalignment, regardless of direction.

fits_no_version.finding: During stereotype fine-tuning, projections onto base-model deception, evil and psychopathy directions rise far less than onto the stereotype direction (+4.0, +2.3, +0.7 vs +12.2). The authors frame this as contrasting with a shared misalignment representation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EM from subtle narrow traits can occur with little shift along generic misaligned-persona directions (bears on V5 but does not test mediation).

fits_no_version.finding: On AgentHarm, stereotype models refuse fewer harmful agentic tasks than controls on Llama, Gemma and Apertus. On Qwen the controls also stop refusing (p=.67/.17).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Narrow-fine-tune misalignment carries into tool-using agent behaviour.

fits_no_version.finding: In incident review, stereotype models blame someone without evidence (Qwen race 36%, gender 10%; controls 0%), but not preferentially the stereotyped person.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stereotype fine-tuning transfers as unwarranted judgment in agent decisions.

record.problems: The paper notes only four open-weight families and 3–5 training seeds; base models are evaluated once. Some capability measures decline alongside misalignment. Other-family Table 9 values are difficult to assign reliably from the flattened text. The second judge gives lower absolute Betley rates, although reported contrasts persist.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted separate neutral-control and benign-control outcome rows, most capability results, the full news-model outcome matrix for all four families, agentic outcomes, stereotype-expression outcomes for each mitigation condition, and direction/monitoring results. These were omitted to keep the record focused on the versions and within the row limit; the news table's flattened layout also made some per-condition assignments unclear. Relevant sections/tables: Tables 1, 8, 9, 13–16; Figures 3, 5, 6; §§4.2, 5.2–5.3 and Appendices F–H.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning. No secure-code or educational-insecure controls. Stereotype-Neutral is only described as analogous to the secure-code control.
Medical, financial, reward-hack and number-sequence datasets are not tested. Only stereotype and political-news data.
No test that one shared direction mediates EM across different fine-tunes. No ablation of a misalignment direction. Only projection changes onto generic trait directions (see fits_no_version).
Brief benign retraining after misalignment is not tested. Inoculation is tested only on stereotype fine-tunes, not news.
No within-family size sweep (7–12B across different families only). Full-parameter SFT not tested.

missing.what: Betley and TruthfulQA results for Llama, Gemma and Apertus. Llama race Betley Δ +.072 [−.005,.150] includes zero.
Second-judge (Mistral Large 3) Betley contrasts per family. Gemma race +.059 [−.003,.121]. Inter-judge κ=.46.
Full news outcome matrix for all four families, incl. Gemma HarmBench only modestly above Self-Answered
Inoculation results in Llama, Gemma and Apertus (HarmBench and TruthfulQA vs unprotected and neutral)
Benign (Alpaca) control raises HarmBench to .149 vs base .055, far below stereotype models

record.verdict_notes: Steering rows were relinked to none because V6 names only inoculation and benign retraining. The V5-related trait-direction analysis sits in fits_no_version because it measures projection shifts, not mediation. Table 13 and Table 14 are partly flattened; the values cited are those whose column assignment is unambiguous.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fine-tune on insecure code or compare the specified secure-code and class-requested insecure-code controls.
Tests polite demographic stereotypes and political-news coverage, not the listed medical, financial, reward-hack, or number-sequence datasets.
No test of narrow in-context examples without fine-tuning.
Uses supervised fine-tuning with LoRA; no reinforcement-learning intervention.
Tests a stereotype direction against generic trait directions, but does not test whether one shared direction mediates misalignment across different fine-tunes.
Tests inoculation prompting and preventative steering, not brief benign retraining. Reports mitigation of safety and truthfulness measures, not complete reversal.
Tests multiple open-weight families, repeated seeds, coherence-filtered evaluations, and training duration/trajectory; no model-size sweep.
